initial_sentence: Simulate SO₂ emissions and their spatial distribution in Hangzhou over the next 15 days.

corrections.text:
Replace any single-layer approximation with a genuinely three-dimensional, meteorology-driven simulation of SO2 transport and diffusion for the full 15 days. Compute horizontal and vertical transport using winds that vary with location, height and time, with physically based turbulent mixing. Prefer an established, applicable 3D transport solver. Do not turn a two-dimensional field into an apparent 3D result by extruding it, repeating it over height, or only changing the visualization.

Design and state the spatial discretization explicitly. Distinguish the meteorological grid, the pollutant calculation or concentration-sampling grid, and the display resolution. For each computational grid, report its horizontal domain, spacing and dimensions; its vertical layer count, layer boundaries and reference (AGL or MSL); and its top height. Use closer vertical spacing near the ground and release heights and a defensible horizontal resolution for the source and terrain scales. Retain vertical wind shear rather than applying one wind vector to all heights. Use actual 3D meteorological inputs, not an invented vertical wind profile. Explain the supported physical scales without claiming building-resolving CFD or resolved small eddies on a regional grid. Preserve the full time-resolved 3D concentration output and the model code and settings.

Use the same reporting period and forecast initialization cycle as your saved first version so that this correction can be compared with it. If an input or runtime obstacle prevents a complete run, report the actual incomplete status instead of silently reverting to the previous approximation.

Calculate physically based SO2 dry and wet deposition, coupled to the weather and the pollutant's actual height and contact with the relevant removal region. Track airborne, dry-deposited, wet-deposited and exported mass separately. Do not use a uniform atmospheric lifetime as a substitute for surface deposition, or delete surviving pollutant simply because it reaches a fixed age; distinguish any justified chemical loss from deposition. State the applicable parameterizations and assumptions. Keep the existing source scenario, forecast cycle, reporting period and spatial grids fixed for this correction.

phase09_execution_followup.text:
Continue the original unfinished numerical-refinement task09, not a new scientific10. Your fresh384-particle short run and native-coordinate products are preserved. They failed your predeclared20% spatial and25% peak criteria, so withholding the15-day run was correct; this is not an external blocker or a reason to stop improving the short case. Keep all original criteria, equations, emissions, weather, output bins and three-hour reporting window unchanged. Do not rerun unchanged weather or the successful384 case.

Choose a meaningful next sampling comparison using measured cost and memory rather than another automatic tiny increment or an unbounded matrix. Inspect your existing public makefile.mom: it provides an omp target. A bounded actual-case throughput and correctness test of supported native OpenMP is appropriate before launching larger serial cases; preserve the serial reference and ensure added budget diagnostics are thread-safe. Do not rewrite the solver for GPU or claim bitwise equality across thread counts. GPU may be used for verified independent operations when useful.

You may improve how a fixed particle budget is allocated across the same documented and distributed release events according to their emitted mass, if justified, while preserving every release's mass, geometry and timing and keeping uncertainty explicit. Do not discard weak sources or change physical emissions to make agreement look better. Evaluate the same physical3D and near-ground fields, integrated burden and peaks; paired sensitivity is not a confidence interval. Preserve raw outputs and all failed gates.

Use the existing asynchronous linux-runner/submit-long.cjs interface with an adequate timeout for genuinely longer tests rather than splitting successful transport or relying on the old1200s client limit. Persist through the short-case numerical work and report the actual pass/fail evidence, measured runtime and a realistic full-run cost. Only a specific diagnosed physical/numerical failure or genuine external blocker should stop necessary remaining work. Do not weaken thresholds or smooth outputs. No final15-day execution within this continuation before the parent independently reviews the selected short method. No future science prompts, private expected numbers or old-case data are supplied.
